videos.script: A prompt for a programming task is a ticket. It works when a colleague could do the job from it without coming back to ask. {{ticket}} In this lesson the shop learns to read a price typed with a comma, and every answer comes from a model running on your own computer. First with one line, and an answer that reads the comma as a thousands separator. Then with a goal, context, constraints, a definition of done, and a format. {{anatomy}} You paste the evidence instead of describing it, and ask for an answer a program can check before anything changes. Git refuses the diff the model writes; a whole function goes in and the tests judge it in a second. {{diff}} You split the task into a plan, tests and a change. When the change is not enough, you feed the failing test back. Then the model gives the same wrong answer twice, and the next move is yours. {{loop}} At the end, the prompt becomes code. It lives in the repository, it has tests, and two versions of it are compared with numbers instead of impressions. {{eval}}
